A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 27-page versions of the same work, including Appendices A-I. Pages 3-27 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the changes on pages 1-2 are fully assessable.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama and Mistral experiments in Table 3, training and token-probability analyses in Figures 2-3, and vocabulary analyses and case studies in Appendix I.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, training analyses, and Appendix I empirical findings.

M1.justification: The NRT objective, reward aggregation schemes, reward stabilization, structural supervision, and training algorithm are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same tulu-3-sft-mixture training data, nine evaluation benchmarks, and Appendix I case-study scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains SFT, JLB, Verifree, RLPR, and the same NRT variants. Comparator participation in the training analyses and appendix case studies is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, training settings, OLMES benchmark protocols, and 100-instance semantic-quality evaluation are unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendices F-H.

E4.justification: The training-dynamics and token-probability analyses in Sections 4.3-4.4 and the vocabulary analyses and case studies in Appendix I are identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the same point estimates and training curves remain.

E6.justification: All reported results are identical. For example, Table 3 retains Llama-3.1-8B overall scores of 56.2 for NRT-WS (-log p), 46.0 for SFT, and 50.8 for RLPR. Figures 2-4 and appendix case-study results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, gradient derivations, and reward aggregation formulas in Section 3 and Appendices B-C are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about verifier-free reasoning, benchmark performance, and resistance to policy collapse.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations concerning handcrafted rewards, sampling costs, and fine-tuning are unchanged. Appendix I.3 retains the same discussion of a hallucinated course recommendation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote stating that code is available and providing the project's GitHub repository address; v1 lacks this pointer. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and research positioning are unchanged. Removing 'predefined' before 'rubric' in Section 2 does not substantively alter the characterization of prior work.

P1.justification: Section 2 changes 'a predefined rubric' to 'a rubric'. v2 also adds the code footnote and updates footnote markers and version text, without reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: The added title footnote and reassigned corresponding-author marker produce small spacing and text-flow changes on pages 1-2. All figures and tables are unchanged, and pages 3-27 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new code-repository pointer modestly improves implementation discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and appendix evidence are unchanged, so the benefit is limited. Repository availability and completeness cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.
